concept.name: Mutual fund
concept.definition: An SEC-registered open-end investment company that pools money from many investors and invests it in stocks, bonds, short-term money-market instruments, other securities, or assets. Its shares are redeemable: investors can sell them back to the fund on any business day at the fund's next-computed net asset value.
concept.intuition: A mutual fund is a shared portfolio: many investors chip in, a manager runs the money to a stated objective, and each investor owns a slice priced once a day.
concept.mechanics: Shares are bought from and redeemed by the fund itself at the net asset value computed after each market close; funds generally must pay redemption proceeds within seven days. Funds may charge sales loads, redemption fees, and ongoing distribution (12b-1) and management fees, all disclosed in the prospectus.
concept.formula: NAV per share = (total value of fund assets - liabilities) / shares outstanding.
concept.failure_modes: Fees and sales loads compound against returns over time. In stressed markets, heavy redemptions can force asset sales into falling prices, and strong past performance frequently reverts, so performance-chasing is unreliable.
concept.misconceptions: That 'no-load' means no fees — no-load funds still charge management and operating expenses. Also, mutual fund shares are not exchange-traded intraday; they transact only at the end-of-day NAV.
concept.example: An investor redeems 500 shares of an equity mutual fund at the day's closing NAV of $24.10 and receives $12,050 within the settlement period.
